newsitem.title: JAPAN: New models boost Japanese car sales.
newsitem.headline: New models boost Japanese car sales.

text.p: Japanese vehicle sales rose in September for the first time in two months and are expected to maintain their upward course, with buyers attracted by an array of new models in the nation's car showrooms.
Industry data released Tuesday showed domestic vehicle sales rose 8.4 percent to 511,911 units in September from a year earlier.

An official from the Japan Automobile Dealers Association, which compiled the data, said domestic sales would remain strong in coming months, helped by demand for new models such as Toyota's Mark II series of luxury cars.

All of Japan's top vehicle makers saw sales rise in September, the first such broad monthly increase since December 1989. The rise, achieved despite only sluggish recovery in Japan's economy, also reflected aggressive selling by dealers keen to have healthy sales figures for the fiscal half year to Sept. 30.

Toyota, Japan's biggest car maker, said it received 43,000 domestic orders for its Mark II and sister models in the first three weeks after it was launched on Sept. 5 with a monthly sales target of 23,500.
A Toyota Motor spokesman said sales of the Mark II were expected to pick up pace in October.
Toyota's domestic sales rose 4.7 percent in September to 181,688, driven by strong customer interest in new models like the Ipsum multi-purpose vehicle, the spokesman said.
Sales at Nissan Motor increased by 0.9 percent to 108,810, helped by good sales of its Cima luxury sedan and March.
Mitsubishi Motors sales rose 16.4 percent to 50,546, buoyed by demand for new models including the Galant and Legnum.
Honda Motor sales rose a healthy 26.3 percent to 45,741 as its recreational vehicles sold well, a Honda spokesman said.

Honda will operate two Japanese plants, in Sayama and Suzuka, for two extra days in October and November to meet demand for various models, including Civics for the European and U.S. markets, as well as to produce its new compact car, the Logo, to be launched Oct. 3.

Mazda Motor attributed a marginal 0.4 percent rise in its sales to demand for its new Demio compact recreational vehicle, its MPV minivan and Sentia luxury sedan. The rise -- taking sales in September to 30,320 units -- was the first year-on-year gain for Mazda since December 1995.
All five major carmakers said they expected to continue to rack up domestic sales gains in October and subsequent months in view of the strong demand for new models.

Japan's overall domestic vehicle sales may rise to 5.20 million units in the year to March 1997, up from 5.17 million a year earlier as buyers snap up new models ahead of a planned rise in Japan's consumption tax, the JADA official said.
The Japanese government plans to raise the consumption tax to 5 percent next April 1 from the present 3 percent.
